title: Worksheet 5: Loop Counters and Increments
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: A loop counter is a variable used to keep track of how many times a loop has repeated, or to track a changing value as a loop progresses through each repetition. Loop counters are typically created before a loop begins, starting at some initial value, and are then updated once during each pass through the loop, a process often called "incrementing" when the value increases or "decrementing" when the value decreases. For example, a loop counter named "count" could start at 0 before a loop begins, and then increase by 1 during each repetition of the loop; after the loop has repeated exactly 4 times, the value stored in "count" would be 4, assuming the counter started at 0 and increased by exactly 1 each time through. If a loop counter is updated incorrectly, such as accidentally increasing it by 2 instead of 1 each time, the counter's final value after the same number of repetitions would end up being different than expected, which can cause a program to behave in ways the programmer did not intend.
